note: upstream_ids are the 105 NFRx.y DEFINED by this unit's five nfr-requirements files, enumerated mechanically rather than transcribed. Every id was checked to appear in the prose of the design document its target names, not merely somewhere in the stage directory: comparing ID sets is the weaker property that let five wrong citations survive a previous stage of this record. D3 MINTS NO NEW ID. A bare NFR20.10, NFR20.11, NFR21.1 or NFR14.15 appearing in a design body is a CITATION of a prior unit's requirement, never a definition here. The BRx.y rows under `business_rules` are the functional-design rules whose mechanism this stage designs; they are cited, not defined. Three designs carry this unit: the collection-number allowlist (NFR14.32), which is NEW WORK because the built schema-wide invariant is one-directional and silent on a teacher-authored field flowing downward; the absence-of-success alert (NFR25.9), designed as a job-written heartbeat row plus a separately-triggered freshness query, which must detect both a scheduler never wired and a cron entry wiped by a deploy; and the refusal-code classification (security-design section 4), which marks each D3 refusal pre-authorization (shared NOT_AVAILABLE) or post-authorization (descriptive), because the built registry test asserts the absence of an oracle-shaped PAIR and cannot catch a new individually-disclosing code.
